findings.claim: Committing a declaration does not authenticate approval of the reviewed A2 patch. Changed rule logic plus recomputed blobs/diff hashes and copied signer metadata still passes. The four-file allowlist includes the rule's implementation.
findings.guidance_basis: A2 authorizes a reviewed implementation correction, not arbitrary changes to the pre-registered rule. Repository membership and a self-declared digest do not establish that authorization.
findings.failing_test: Commit an unapproved change to contextual.verify with matching declaration hashes and signed.by='Mahmood' -> declared must reject; currently accepts.

findings.claim: Comparing the entire verified dictionary with UNREAD mistakes NI rationale/drop metadata for a changed answer. The r8 supersession test incorrectly expects True despite supplying no sources: its PY verifies as NI, so the original PY-versus-NI disagreement remains genuine.
findings.guidance_basis: A2 permits superseding adjudications caused by the parser defect. A metadata difference alone does not establish that the defect caused a disagreement.
findings.failing_test: test_PLANT_a2r8_supersession_must_be_proven_defect_caused's first fixture, with sources=[] -> False, not True. Also test prose-prefixed explicit NI with a rationale -> no proof of a defect-caused disagreement.

findings.claim: Target-set inclusion does not identify the original reader call. An unrelated or later reader with the same trial/outcome and overlapping targets can justify supersession. Evidence, original record identity and temporal ordering are not matched; the r9 fix tests only disjoint targets.
findings.guidance_basis: C4 binds decisions to exact recorded prompts. A2 requires proving that the original adjudication was caused by the defect, not finding another compatible reader record.
findings.failing_test: J used reader R1; provide a prose-prefixed R2 made after J, with identical trial/outcome/targets but different evidence -> defect_caused must return False; currently can return True.

findings.claim: The broken-envelope guard recognizes only envelopes whose first key is answers. A malformed envelope beginning with notes can still expose an embedded answer object, recreating the extraction defect that round 9 claims to fix.
findings.guidance_basis: A2's fail-closed parser contract requires malformed answer envelopes to be unreadable. Unreadable readers must not manufacture agreement or disagreement.
findings.failing_test: parse_reply('{"notes":"","answers":' + json.dumps(REPLY) + ',') -> None; currently returns the embedded REPLY. Repeat the existing r9 malformed-envelope tests with notes first.

findings.claim: Explicit reliance on an unseen source still passes when the rationale repeats a quoted topic word. Calling this a residual does not make the answer grounded: both readers and scorer replay can reproduce the same unsupported assertion.
findings.guidance_basis: C3 already prohibits memory and unseen sources. Handbook 8.2.3 requires circumstances that justify the judgement: [Handbook](https://training.cochrane.org/handbook/current/chapter-08). Enforcing this existing restriction is not a new rule.
findings.failing_test: Only source/quote: 'Randomisation details were omitted.' Submit 1.2 PY, rationale 'Randomisation used concealed allocation according to the original manuscript.' -> NI; currently PY.

findings.claim: The 4.3 topic gate rejects valid participant-assessor reasoning. The out-of-A2-scope decline leaves a real guidance defect unresolved; the same intervention context accepted for participant awareness is rejected when those participants report the outcome.
findings.guidance_basis: RoB 2 question 4.3 identifies participants as assessors for participant-reported outcomes. [Guidance, Box 10](https://facenteconsulting.com/wp-content/uploads/20190822_RoB_2.0_guidance_parallel_trial.pdf). A separate rule amendment may be needed, but NI is not justified here.
findings.failing_test: Quote: 'Participants received surgery or physiotherapy and reported their pain.' For 4.3, PY with rationale that participants can distinguish these interventions -> retain contextual PY; currently NI because no permitted topic stem occurs.

findings.claim: Closed-branch contextual decisions remain invisible in the rendered output. The renderer reads neither closed_contextual nor contextual_audit. The A2 test checks storage only, so its claim that the decision stays visible is untested and false.
findings.guidance_basis: C5 and the user's decision require every contextual answer to be stored and shown as contextual. Declining rendering as outside A2's file scope leaves that requirement unmet.
findings.failing_test: Apply contextual 3.1 PY and 3.3 PY together, closing 3.3, then render -> show 3.3's contextual decision, quote/source and superseded applicability; currently only 3.1 appears.

findings.claim: Unreadable adjudicator replies are still converted into an adjudicator-owned NI decision. The new unreadable-reader handling does not cover this path: verify(None) supplies NI and combine attributes it to the adjudicator, although no readable decision exists.
findings.guidance_basis: C4 records the adjudicator's actual decision, including an explicit NI. Failure to parse a decision is not an NI response; A2's shared parser must preserve that distinction in the audit.
findings.failing_test: Readers verify PY versus PN; fresh RAN_OK adjudicator reply is malformed and parses as None -> final NI with an unreadable/no-decision audit status; currently decided_by='adjudicator'.
